views.note: The old daemon accepts, then tears down every socket.

views.label: Handover
views.note: It writes state and log rings, then execs the new binary.

views.label: Rehydrate
views.note: The new daemon rebuilds sessions and replays the exact gap.

messages.label: write versioned state + rings
messages.note: clear FD_CLOEXEC on each master fd

messages.label: execv(serve --takeover)
messages.note: same PID; PTY children keep running

cards.title: Quiesce
items: The endpoint answers 200 before teardown, so a caller inside a pane gets its reply
Teardown runs on the single event loop, so no reader races it
Bytes not yet read stay in the kernel PTY buffer and survive exec

cards.title: Handover
items: Only the master fds and the session state cross the boundary
FD_CLOEXEC is cleared just before exec and set again after adoption
The old binary writes the versioned state; the new binary reads it

cards.title: Rehydrate
items: The new daemon rebuilds each PtySession around its inherited fd
The ring came across, so ?since hits the exact-gap path (resync=0)
Every failure degrades to today's upgrade --restart or better
